newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures close heftily lower.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures close heftily lower.

text.p: IMM currency futures posted another session of hefty losses at the close as dollar strength persisted.
Mild profit-taking in the dollar on upticks kept key currencies above their contract lows set in GLOBEX overnight trade, but the overall tone was dismal for currencies.

March marks, Swiss francs and yen all stumbled to another set of lows overnight as the dollar surged to key psychological levels, with dollar targets seen at 120 to 125 yen and 1.57 marks. March sterling collapsed to the lowest price since early December in panicky afternoon trade.
One IMM trader said heavy sell-stops were triggered at $1.6560 that sparked a wave of panic selling.
"It just kept tanking," the trader said. Support in March sterling for Thursday was seen at $1.6300, a three-month low settlement from December 5.
March marks and Swiss francs ended just above their pit session lows set late in the day, while March yen posted a new contract low late in pit trade.
"Basically, nobody wants to be short dollars," one IMM currency trader said. "Even if you see some (dollar) profittaking, you still have to buy dollars," he recommended.
Comments from Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke spawned a bit of confusion in currencies, as traders said his comments could be interpreted several ways.

He said he sees no inflationary dangers from the dollar's appreciation. Welteke also said the mark's slide versus the dollar must slow, but added that the mark's depreciation had helped boost German exports.
Early in the day, traders cited comments from a French parliamentarian suggesting that Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet may expect the dollar to rise further.
